{{Quote|You were right about one thing, Master. The negotiations were short.|Obi-wan Kenobi to Qui-Gon Jinn after escaping the Federation's ambush|<ref name="TPM" />}}
Following the [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] ambassadors [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] were dispatched on a '''Mission to Naboo''' by [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] to resolve the [[Standard month/Legends|month]]-long blockade. They secretly traveled aboard the [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class cruiser]] [[Radiant VII/Legends|Radiant VII]], where they were greeted in the [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']] in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] around Naboo by the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[TC-14/Legends|TC-14]]. While Jinn and Kenobi waited in a conference room, TC-14 informed the [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] that the Republic had sent Jedi.

Gunray felt threatened and consulted [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], the secret mastermind of the blockade. Sidious ordered the Jedi to be [[Death/Legends|killed]] and for the Trade Federation to begin landing their troops on Naboo. They began by destroying the docked ''Radiant VII'', killing crewmembers [[Maoi Madakor/Legends|Maoi Madakor]] and [[Antidar Williams/Legends|Antidar Williams]]. Jinn and Kenobi [[Force sense/Legends|sensed]] the ship's destruction and noticed [[Dioxis/Legends|dioxis]] gas filling the conference room, holding their breaths to survive the [[Poison/Legends|poison]]. A group of [[OOM-series battle droid/Legends|OOM-series battle droids]] arrived at the conference room and were instructed by Gunray to deal with the Jedi's remains. Instead, Jinn and Kenobi emerged and began cutting down the [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]]. They quickly headed for the bridge entrance, where Jinn began cutting through the [[Blast door/Legends|blast door]] with his [[Qui-Gon Jinn's lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]].

Their attempted intrusion was interupted by the arrival of two [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]] who immiediately fired upon the Jedi. Recognizing that they could not penetrate the [[Droid/Legends|droids']] [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]], Jinn and Kenobi escaped into the ventilation shaft. They emerged to see the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]] preparing to land on Naboo, and snuck into separate transports so they could meet on the world's surface. The Jedi eventually arrived in [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], Naboo's [[Capital/Legends|capital]], to [[Capture of Theed/Legends|rescue]] [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]], who was dismayed to learn that the negotiations to end the blockade had never occurred.

==Prelude==
===The Sith scheme===
{{Quote|I suggest we strike at the homeworld of the senator who was most responsible for championing the taxation bill: Naboo.|Darth Sidious, manipulating the Trade Federation leadership into blockading Naboo|<ref name="Cloak of Deception">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Saakak-TPM.png|thumb|left|300px|The Trade Federation stationed a battle fleet around Naboo, led by the flagship ''Saak'ak''.]]
The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], known publicly as [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] Palpatine of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], sought to dominate [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] to complete the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Grand Plan/Legends|Grand Plan]]. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], Palpatine convinced [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]]<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> to support the passage of [[Senate Resolution BR-0371]], which resulted in a loss of profits for the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]],<ref name="The Essential Chronology">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> but also allowed them to significantly expand a [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]].<ref name="Cloak of Deception" />

The [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] was secretly under the sway of Sidious, who convinced [[Gender/Legends|him]] to [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in response to BR-0371, preferably [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], his own [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> Six [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the passage of BR-0371, the Trade Federation launched the blockade of Naboo, halting all commerce to the world<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" /> by surrounding it with a battle fleet of [[Lucrehulk-class LH-3210 cargo freighter/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class LH-3210 cargo freighters]], including the [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']], which served as the [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]].<ref name="Complete Cross Sections">''[[Star Wars: Complete Cross-Sections]]''</ref> The Sith and Neimoidians' eventual goal was to invade the planet itself with the Droid Army,<ref name="TPM" /> convincing [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of Naboo to sign a treaty relinquishing the planet and its [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]] reserves to the Trade Federation.<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> The Trade Federation leadership believed that Amidala would quickly capitulate, creating an example that would intimidate other worlds, but she refused.<ref name="TPM junior novel">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' junior novelization]]</ref>

===Valorum's ambassadors===
{{Quote|With all due respect, the ambassadors of the Supreme Chancellor wish to board immediately."<br />"Yes, of course. As you know our blockade is perfectly legal, and we'd be happy to receive the ambassadors.|Captain Maoi Madakor transmitting to Viceroy Nute Gunray|<ref name="TPM" />|audio=MadakorAndGunray.flac}}
[[File:Radiant_VII_docked.png|thumb|right|350px|Chancellor Valorum dispatched the ''Radiant VII'' to transport Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi to resolve the blockade of Naboo.]]
Naboo's circumstances were debated endlessly by the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]<ref name="TPM" /> for close to a month. At that [[Time/Legends|time]], Queen Amidala communicated via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] with Valorum, explaining that she held him personally responsible for the suffering of her [[Naboo (people)|Naboo]].<ref name="Episode I Journal: Queen Amidala">''[[Star Wars Journal: Queen Amidala]]''</ref> The chancellor chose to break protocol through private action, using his [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] friend [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]] to request aid from the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] without informing the Senate. [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] dispatched Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to negotiate with the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] to bring an end to the blockade.<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> Valorum informed Amidala that he had sent Jedi [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassadors]] to deal with the blockade.<ref name="Episode I Journal: Queen Amidala" />

Valorum prepared a dossier for Jinn to provide intelligence on Naboo and the Trade Federation. In it, he expressed a concern that an armed conflict with the Trade Federation could destablize the galactic community, and that he suspected a hidden influence behind the blockade that he hoped would reveal itself. He also hoped the Jedi reputation would frighten the Neimoidian's into compliance.<ref name="Secrets of Naboo">{{WizCite|book=Secrets of Naboo|story=A Letter from Chancellor Valorum}}</ref> Jinn and Kenobi traveled to Naboo<ref name="TPM" /> aboard the [[Radiant VII/Legends|''Radiant VII'']], a [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class cruiser]] which, given the sensitive nature of the mission, was piloted by a skeleton crew<ref name="Vehicles and Vessels">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> consisting of [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]] personnel [[Antidar Williams/Legends|Antidar Williams]] and [[Maoi Madakor/Legends|Maoi Madakor]].<ref name="Antidar">{{DB|character|ltwilliams|Williams, Lt. Antidar}}</ref>

==The Mission==
===The Jedi arrive===
{{Quote|Is it in their nature to make us wait this long?"<br />"No, I sense an unusual amount of fear for something as trivial as this trade dispute.|Kenobi and Jinn|<ref name="TPM" />|audio=TrivialTradeDispute-TPM.flac}}
[[File:TC-14_distraction.png|thumb|left|280px|The Jedi wait for negotiations to start]]
As they approached the ''Saak'ak'', Madakor communicated with Gunray via transmission that the Jedi wished to board the vessel, and the viceroy stated that he would happily receive the ambassadors.<ref name="TPM" /> Jinn could already [[Force sense/Legends|sense]] the nervousness of the Neimoidians through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="TPM junior novel" /> Once the ''Radiant VII'' had landed, Jinn pondered to Kenobi why the Trade Federation had selected Naboo receiving no answer.<ref name="TPM novel">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref> The Jedi were greeted by the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[TC-14/Legends|TC-14]], who led them to a conference room before leaving to retrieve Gunray. Kenobi shared his unease with his master, [[Force sense/Legends|sensing]] through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] that something was wrong. Jinn assured him that he needed to focus away from his anxieties, and that he expected the cowardly Neimoidians to quickly resolve their issues.<ref name="TPM" />

TC-14 informed Gunray and [[Daultay Dofine/Legends|Daultay Dofine]] that the ambassadors were Jedi, causing both to panic. Gunray ordered Dofine to distract the Jedi while he contacted Sidious, an order Dofine refused, insisting that TC-14 rejoin the Jedi instead. TC-14 arrived in the conference room with beverages for the Jedi, and Kenobi questioned the time they had spent waiting while Jinn sensed an unusually high level of fear in the Neimoidians.<ref name="TPM" /> In a meeting on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] with his [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]], [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], Sidious received word from Valorum that the Jedi had been sent to Naboo. Both were concerned, believing the Neimoidians could panic and reveal Sith's intentions, and knew that Jinn and Kenobi were cause for concern, as they had interupted previous Sith schemes.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

===Sith orders===
{{Quote|The chancellor should never have brought them into this. Kill them immediately.|Darth Sidious ordering Nute Gunray to kill the Jedi|<ref name="TPM" />}}
Sidious assured Plagueis that the two were no much for the thousands of [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] at the Trade Federation's disposal, and that he would order Gunray to [[Death/Legends|kill]] them. Plagueis believed that Jinn could hide and wreak havoc on the ''Saak'ak'', so Sidious concluded that they would commence the invasion ahead of schedule, changing the Jedi's objectives from [[Prisoner/Legends|arresting]] the Neimoidians to protecting the Naboo.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> The Neimoidians conferred with Sidious via hologram, Gunray was unsure of the course of action, knowing the Jedi would not have Senate approval for the mission,<ref name="TEA" /> while Dofine's fear of the Jedi led him to claim that the scheme had already failed. Sidious dismissed Dofine and ordered Gunray to begin the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], assuring him that he could guarantee the invasion's legality. Gunray questioned what was to be done with the Jedi, and Sidious stated that the chancellor should not have involved them, ordering their [[Death/Legends|deaths]].<ref name="TPM" />

[[File:Sidious-talks-to-Federation.png|thumb|right|300px|Sidious orders the deaths of Jinn and Kenobi]]
Gunray immediately ordered Haako to destroy the ''Radiant VII'' and sent a squad of battle droids to deal with the Jedi.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Sidious's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], who had watched the transmission, asked his master whether he truly believed the Neimoidians could kill the Jedi, and Sidious responded that even fools such as the Neimoidians could get lucky. Maul knew that the Neimoidians would fail and hoped that he would be summoned to battle the Jedi in order to prove himself.<ref name="Maul Journal">''[[Star Wars Journal: Darth Maul]]''</ref>

===The ambush===
{{Quote|Check it out, corporal. We'll cover you.''"<br />"''Roger roger.|OWO-1 and and an OOM security droid corporal before entering the conference room to ambush the Jedi|<ref name="TPM" />}}
[[File:OWO1-squad-final-moments.png|thumb|left|280px|The battle droids discover that the Jedi are still alive]]
Gunray pressed a button to view the hangar where the ''Radiant VII'' was docked, and barely hesitated to activate the hangar's [[Autoturret/Legends|autoturret]].<ref name="TPM junior novel" /> Williams and Madakor noticed the turret turning towards them, but were unable to raise their [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]] in time and were killed by turretfire,<ref name="TPM" /> along with additional manual fire by the droid [[OWO-3]] ordered by gunner [[Jull Dremon]],<ref name="Insider 147 Neimoidians">{{InsiderCite|147|Rogues Gallery|Rogues Gallery: The Devious Neimoidians Revealed}}"</ref> which destroyed the ''Radiant VII''. Jinn and Kenobi immediately sensed the disturbance and drew their [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], before noticing that the room was being flooded with poisonous [[Dioxis/Legends|dioxis]] gas,<ref name="TPM" /> which killed the [[Pylat bird/Legends|Neimoidian pylat birds]] on display in the conference room.<ref name="TPM novel" /> The Jedi began holding their breaths. A group of ten [[OOM-series battle droid/Legends|OOM-series battle droids]] marched to the conference room, where Gunray ordered them via hologram to destroy what remained of the Jedi.<ref name="TPM" />

The programming of one of the droids, [[SSA-1015]], assured him that the Jedi could be defeated.<ref name="SSA-1015" /> Once the droids opened the door, TC-14 emerged, apologizing for her interuption<ref name="TPM" /> as she escaped into the corridor.<ref name="TC-14">{{FactFile|71|TEE 1-4|TC-14}}</ref> The droid leader [[OWO-1/Legends|OWO-1]]<ref name="OWO-1" /> ordered a [[Unidentified OOM-series security droid corporal/Legends|corporal]] to investigate, but first they saw the activated lightsabers and began firing with their [[E-5 blaster rifle/Legends|E-5 blaster rifles]]. Jinn and Kenobi quickly cut down the droids, slashing through them, deflecting their fire, and using the Force to push three of them down. Panicking at the loss of transmission from the droids, Gunray ordered the bridge of the ''Saak'ak'' sealed off and called for [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]] to deal with the Jedi. Haako expressed doubt that he and Gunray would survive the hostile encounter.<ref name="TPM" />

===The Jedi retreat===
{{Quote|Where are those droidekas?|Nute Gunray, growing frantic as Jinn cuts through the bridge's blast door|<ref name="TPM" />}}
[[File:Destroyers_attacking_Jedi.png|thumb|right|300px|Jinn and Kenobi under fire by droidekas]]
In only [[Standard second|seconds]], Jinn and Kenobi made their way to the bridge, acting as a seemingly unstoppable force able to anticipate their opponents attacks.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Jinn began cutting through the doorway with his lightsaber while Kenobi cut down approaching battle droids. Gunray had the [[Blast door/Legends|blast door]] activated, believing it would hold them, but Jinn's lightsaber was still able to pierce the door.<ref name="TPM" /> The bridge crew stared transfixed as the blast door melted away, leading to various mutterings until Gunray screamed for silence.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Just as Haako complained about the lack of droidekas, two units,<ref name="TPM" /> the leader [[P-59]] and subordinate [[P-60]],<ref name="P-60" /> rolled up behind the Jedi and began rapidly firing on them.<ref name="TPM" /> Jinn sensed their arrival<ref name="TPM novel" /> was forced to withdraw from the door to help Kenobi block their fire, and the Jedi realized that they could not breach the droid's shields. They used the Force to [[Force speed/Legends|speed]] away, escaping behind the droids and into a ventilation shaft.<ref name="TPM" />

The droidekas switched to biological scanners, allowing them to spot the Jedi as they entered the shaft.<ref name="TPM comic">[[Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace 1|''Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace'' 1]]</ref> Haako was scarcely able to believe that they had survived, and Gunray stood in disbelief at the Jedi's involvement,<ref name="TPM novel" /> believing they were impossible to kill.<ref name="Who">''[[Star Wars Episode I Who's Who: A Pocket Guide to the Characters of The Phantom Menace]]''</ref> It did not occur to the droids to search the service vents as a team of [[Human/Legends|Humans]] would have, which Jinn was thankful for as he and Kenobi crept through them.<ref name="TPM junior novel" /> When they emerged in the ''Saak'ak{{'s}}'' hangar, Jinn and Kenobi saw the ruins of the ''Radiant VII'',<ref name="Movie storybook">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Movie Storybook|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace Movie Storybook'']]</ref> and the Droid Army preparing for the surface invasion, considering it an odd play for the Trade Federation to make. Jinn instructed Kenobi to stow aboard [[Unidentified C-9979 landing craft|separate]] [[C-9979 landing craft/Legends|C-9979 landing crafts]], hoping to warn the Naboo and Chancellor Valorum about the invasion. Kenobi joked that his master had been right about the length of the negotiations.<ref name="TPM" />

===The invasion begins===
{{Quote|This turn of events is unfortunate. We must accelerate our plans. Begin landing your troops.''"<br />"''My lord, is that&hellip;''legal''?''"<br />"''I will ''make it'' legal.|Darth Sidious gives orders to Nute Gunray|<ref name="TPM" />}}
[[File:Trade_Federation_Invasion.png|thumb|left|300px|Jinn and Kenobi's mission triggered the Invasion of Naboo early]]
Queen Amidala connected with the ''Saak'ak'' via transmission, believing that the blockade had been resolved by the ambassadors. Gunray denied that they had arrived and lied that Amidala had been mistaken. Amidala told Gunray that he had gone too far, and he responded that the Trade Federation would not act without Senate approval. Haako told Gunray that the queen was right and questioned whether she suspected an attack. Gunray was unsure, but ordered that communications on Naboo be disrupted immediately.<ref name="TPM" />

To that end, Gunray dispatched the [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droid]] [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]] to land on Naboo ahead of the rest of the Droid Army to [[Subjugation of Parrlay|disable]] transmitters that would have allowed Naboo to spread word of the invasion to the Republic.<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds" /> In a meeting of the [[Naboo Royal Advisory Council/Legends|Naboo Royal Advisory Council]], Amidala communicated the ambassador's lack of presence to Palpatine via hologram, which Palpatine claimed to be shocked to hear based on assurances from the chancellor. Naboo [[Governor of Naboo/Legends|Governor]] [[Sio Bibble/Legends|Sio Bibble]] realized that a disruption could only mean a forthcoming invasion. Amidala hoped that negotiations would be able to save the Naboo, while the rest of her [[Advisor/Legends|advisors]] were doubtful.<ref name="TPM" />

===The landing===
{{Quote|Do you think she suspects an attack?''"<br />"''I don't know, but we must move quickly to disrupt all communications down there.|Rune Haako and Nute Gunray, following a transmission with Queen Amidala|<ref name="TPM" />}}
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)}}
During Kenobi's voyage down to the planet, he disrupted the ship's communications so as not to reveal his presence. The disruption attracted the attention of the rest of the ship, and [[Battle droid squad 8313]] was sent to investigate, forcing Kenobi to eliminate the squad. Moving through to the [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tank]] storage bay, he contacted Jinn, who ordered him to either the main control room or the turbine room in order to force the ship to crash-land. Kenobi fought his way through to the turbine room and disabled the turbines. He then went to the main control room and cut down all the present battle droids. He then disabled the [[Holoprojector/Legends|holoprojector]] and went down the hole to the lower level and proceeded to the [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|Multi-Troop Transport]] bay, where he fought and destroyed a [[Trade Federation assassin droid|new type of assassin droid]] armed with a [[Cortosis sword/Legends|cortosis blade]]. After the droid was destroyed, Jinn ordered Kenobi to hide until he landed.<ref name="Obi-Wan">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref>
{{Endgame}}

The Trade Federation's landing craft were deployed in groups of three to cut off the Naboo cities from each other.<ref name="Complete Vis Dic">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Among the transports was [[TT-6]], which carried the majority of the officer battle droids,<ref name="TT-6">{{CCG|set=Theed Palace Limited|cardname=TT-6}}</ref> and [[TT-9]], an auxiliary mobile supply transport.<ref name="TT-9">{{CCG|set=Theed Palace Limited|cardname=TT-9}}</ref> The Neimoidians searched the ''Saak'ak'' for the Jedi, realizing that they must have escaped onboard a landing craft. They transmitted to OOM-9, ordering him to continue searching, and the droid responded that they would be found if they were present.<ref name="TPM" />

===In the swamps===
{{Dialogue|Qui-Gon Jinn|Do you hear that?|Jar Jar Binks|Yeah|Qui-Gon Jinn|That is the sound of a thousand terrible things headed this way. |Obi-Wan Kenobi|If they find us, they will crush us, grind us into tiny pieces and BLAST us into oblivion! |Jar Jar Binks|Hmmm... yousa point is well seen. This way. Hurry!|attr=The two Jedi convince Binks to take them to Otoh Gunga|src=<ref name="TPM" />}}
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)}}
When they landed on the surface, Kenobi and Jinn were separated. Kenobi hid in the [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] and swam to the shore, where he faced a squad of B1 battle droids. After dispatching them, he hid in the water again. He then met a [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] named [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]]. The two ran away from Federation [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Trooper Aerial Platform]]s, and Kenobi fell into the [[Swamp/Legends|swamp]] water. Once back on land, he was used a pushed a stump to climb on top of a log where Binks was perched. The Gungan ran off, and Kenobi followed. Kenobi destroyed the droids in his way. He then jumped into the water; when he got back on land he faced more battle droids in his way around a stuck Multi-Troop Transport. He jumped around a series of small islands in the swamp to avoid the [[Tee/Legends|carnivorous fish]]. Kenobi found Binks again and asked if he had seen his master. Binks said yes and led the young Jedi away. Kenobi tried to follow the Gungan and got stuck in a pit. He got out by pushing a stump to where he could climb out and grab a vine to climb across to the other side. He followed Binks to a droid staging area, and took hold of a [[heavy repeating cannon]] to blast two destroyer droids. After that, Binks led him back to Jinn.<ref name="TPM game">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref>
{{Endgame}}

[[File:Jar_Jar_meets_Jedi.png|thumb|right|300px|Kenobi and Jinn met the Gungan Jar Jar Binks on Naboo.]]
Jinn saw Binks in the path of a Multi-Troop Transport and tackled him to the ground, saving the Gungan's life. As Jinn chastised Binks for his clumsiness, Kenobi ran towards them, pursued by two [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Trooper Aerial Platforms]], which Jinn destroyed by deflecting their fire into them. Kenobi and Jinn persuaded Binks to help them, and the Gungan lead them into the swamps In the meantime, Gunray and Haako communicated with Sidious, where they chose to avoid telling him about the missing Jedi.<ref name="TPM" />

By the time Kenobi reunited with Jinn, his [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's first lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] had shorted out.<ref name="TPM novel" /> After traveling through the swamps, Binks led the two Jedi into the water of the swamps and into [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], the Gungan capital. There they were brought before [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]] and his advisors. Jinn used a [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trick]] to convince Nass to lend them a [[Tribubble bongo/Legends|Tribubble bongo]] and a path to Theed. Nass agreed and told them to travel through the planet's core. Jinn was also able to free Binks, who was going to be punished for returning from his exile. Binks and the two Jedi were able to navigate through the porous core and end up near Theed, surfacing on the [[Solleu River/Legends|Solleu River]].<ref name="TPM" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|We're ambassadors for the Supreme Chancellor.''"<br />"''Your negotiations seem to have failed.''"<br />"''The negotiations never took place.|Qui-Gon Jinn and Sio Bibble after the former rescued Queen Amidala|<ref name="TPM" />}}
[[File:TPM_Cast.png|thumb|right|250px|Jinn and Kenobi eventually met with the Naboo leadership, where they revealed what had become of their negotiations.]]
The morning after their landing,<ref name="Inside">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]''</ref> the Droid Army [[Capture of Theed/Legends|captured]] Theed with relative ease and escorted Amidala and her entourage from [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Theed Royal Palace]]. While battle droids escorted them to [[Camp Four/Legends|Camp Four]], Jinn and Kenobi mounted a rescue, revealing that they were the chancellor's ambassadors and that the negotiations were prevented. The Jedi planned to escort Amidala to Coruscant to testify on the Trade Federation's crimes, eventually doing so after a delay forced them to land on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] for some time.<ref name="TPM" /> During the Fall of Theed, a rumor spread among refugees fleeing the city that the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] had sent a [[Platoon/Legends|platoon]] of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Knights]] to storm the blockade, but they had been captured.<ref name="Secrets">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref> TC-14's regularly scheduled memory wipe was scheduled earlier than usual to hide any evidence of the incident from the Senate, but she was destroyed aboard the [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|''Vuutun Palaa'']] in the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] before it took place.<ref name="TC-14" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Mission to Naboo was created as the opening action scene for the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], written and directed by [[George Lucas]]. It first appeared in the film's [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]] by [[Terry Brooks]],<ref name="TPM novel" /> released on [[April 21]], [[1999]] before the film's premiere on [[May 19]], of that year.<ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> Early concept art for the film by [[Doug Chiang]] portrayed Kenobi alone meeting with the Trade Federation aboard their battleship, as Jinn had not been integrated into the story.<ref name="Art">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]''</ref> The [[Star Wars Insider 42|forty-second issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'', released in February/March of 1999, revealed a shot of the Jedi approaching Naboo and hinted that their investigation was about to turn deadly.<ref name="Insider 42">{{InsiderCite|42|Prequel Update}}</ref> The mission was first identified in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Phantom Menace: The Expanded Visual Dictionary]]''.<ref name="Expand">''[[Star Wars: The Phantom Menace: The Expanded Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

Former [[Marvel Comics|Marvel]] [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'' comics]] editor [[Mary Jo Duffy]] described the scene as her favorite moment of the prequels, acknowledging that it took her back to being a rabid ''Star Wars'' fan.<ref name="Insider 147 Prequels">{{InsiderCite|147|50 Greatest Reasons to Love the Star Wars Prequels!|50 Greatest Reasons to Love the ''Star Wars'' Prequels!}}</ref>

===Inconsistencies===
In the film, two droidekas attack the Jedi,<ref name="TPM" /> but the numbers vary across different sources. In the novelization<ref name="TPM novel" /> and [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Movie Storybook|movie storybook]], ten droidekas arrive to attack Jinn and Kenobi,<ref name="Movie Storybook">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Movie Storybook|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace Movie Storybook'']]</ref> and in the [[Star Wars: Episode I — The Phantom Menace 1|comic]] five roll in.<ref name="TPM comic" />

In both novelizations, Jinn and Kenobi hide from the droidekas after detecting their presence,<ref name="TPM novel" /><ref name="TPM junior novel" /> rather than using the Force to escape immediately as portrayed in the film.<ref name="TPM" />
